tasks.short: Explain which advertising formats suit a customer's goals and why.

steps.what: Review customer goals and campaign history in the {CRM}.
Read media descriptions and prepare explanations suited to the customer's objectives.

loop.input: Customer context and approved media descriptions and performance evidence.
loop.output: Cited talking points explaining relevant formats and their limitations.
loop.check: Require a source for each factual claim; distinguish observed results from forecasts.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported claims or missing evidence return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply facts, but adapting explanations to varied customer goals needs language interpretation.

steps.what: Choose suitable formats and assess trade-offs against the customer's objectives.
Explain the recommendation, answer objections and agree realistic expectations with the customer.
Send the customer a written recommendation and agreed next steps.

tasks.design: Configure a customer context view in the {CRM} and use a bounded drafting loop over approved material in the {DOCS}. The seller chooses the recommendation and conducts the conversation; a configured {EMAIL} template assembles selected formats, expectations and next steps for approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Media descriptions, customer history and supporting results sit in separate places. Tailoring an explanation still takes reading and writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views and templates handle assembly. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while a bounded model call can draft cited explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Advertising outcomes depend on creative quality, audience and execution. Evidence may be weak or incomparable, and confident wording can overstate effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's actual constraints, challenge unrealistic expectations and earn trust while explaining uncertain outcomes.

ambition.what: Review the channel mix at each campaign milestone using fresh results.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time finding and rewriting product facts and more time discussing trade-offs. No new commercial decision rights arise automatically.

reach.task: Validate tracking and delivery requirements for a proposed advertising format.
reach.learn: Measurement limits, attribution assumptions and technical feasibility checks.

evidence.claim: Approved-document retrieval, cited explanations and human handoff are plausible support patterns; recommendation quality remains unproven here.
Teamleader combines customer records and quotes, with its Focus AI acting after approval; this supports the gated workflow pattern.

assumptions: The baseline represents a typical mid-size European advertising seller, not a measured customer workflow.
Conversation remains the largest time component, consistent with the supplied priors.
Approved media descriptions and usable performance evidence exist.
Build ranges are working effort, not elapsed procurement or consultation time; shared foundations reduce duplication across tasks.
No call recording or employee scoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which media formats are sold and how current their evidence is.
Whether the {CRM} supports the required views and approved email templates.
The lawful basis, access permissions and retention rules for customer information.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which explanation claims can be traced to approved evidence?
Does the preparation aid reduce time without increasing unsupported promises?
new_work: Review drafted talking points and outbound summaries.
Maintain approved claims, evidence dates and media descriptions.
Handle customer situations that do not fit the available evidence.
Maintain access controls and source links.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver advertising sales presentations that win or expand customer business.

steps.what: Collect account history, campaign results and opportunity details from the {CRM}.
Adapt approved presentation material to the customer's goals and proposed advertising programme.

loop.input: Presentation facts, approved slides, performance evidence and customer objectives.
loop.output: A populated presentation with tailored narrative and source references.
loop.check: Validate figures against source fields; restrict claims to approved evidence; check required slides and layout.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing evidence or failed layout checks go to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can populate figures, but tailoring the narrative across varied customer briefs needs language drafting.

steps.what: Review the proposal, claims and presentation narrative before customer use.
Arrange the presentation with customer stakeholders.
Present the programme, explore objections and agree the next commercial discussion.
Record customer reactions and follow-up commitments in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Pull presentation facts from the {CRM} into approved templates in the {DOCS}, with deterministic figure checks and one bounded narrative-drafting loop. Configure booking through the {CALENDAR} and a short outcome form in the {CRM}; the seller approves the presentation and leads the customer discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sellers repeatedly copy facts into decks, while customer-specific storytelling makes a single fixed presentation inadequate.
tasks.enabler_now: Document generation and record integration handle repeatable assembly. Bounded drafting can adapt approved material without giving a model control of the sale.
tasks.still_hard: A persuasive presentation depends on stakeholder priorities, credible evidence and handling objections live. Poor source data still produces a weak deck.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, build a persuasive commercial story and adapt the discussion when stakeholders disagree.

ambition.what: Offer tailored campaign reviews to smaller existing advertisers previously receiving only generic materials.

tasks.altitude: The seller arrives with more preparation time available for stakeholder strategy and rehearsal. Presentation support does not expand discount or contract authority.

reach.task: Plan stakeholder coverage for an account expansion.
reach.learn: Buying-group mapping, executive sponsorship and opportunity qualification.

evidence.claim: Customer-record-filled templates and bounded drafting can support sales materials; this digest provides no measured presentation case.
Human delivery remains the largest component of this task; deck automation alone does not automate the customer discussion.

assumptions: Approved presentation templates and reusable campaign evidence exist.
Live delivery remains the majority of time, consistent with the supplied priors.
Booking is limited to seller-selected contacts and offered time slots.
The seller enters meeting outcomes directly; recording and transcription are unnecessary.
Build ranges assume reuse of shared customer-data connections.
unknowns: How much presentation material is reusable and approved.
Whether campaign results can be reliably linked to customer records.
Which booking and document-generation features are already available.
Which employee consultation and access approvals apply under national rules.
research_questions: Which deck sections require tailoring and which should remain fixed?
Can generated decks pass factual and visual checks with a single repair pass?
new_work: Review generated narratives, charts and claims.
Maintain presentation templates and approved examples.
Resolve missing or inconsistent campaign figures.
Keep stakeholder lists and outcome-form fields useful.

tasks.short: Research customer products, needs and advertising history to prepare relevant recommendations.

steps.what: Retrieve account details, previous purchases and advertising history from the {CRM}.
Study customer product material, previous briefs and campaign reports.

loop.input: Authorised customer documents, campaign reports and account facts.
loop.output: Source-linked research notes, contradictions, unknowns and proposed discovery questions.
loop.check: Require source locations for facts; label hypotheses; flag conflicting dates, figures and objectives.
loop.stop: Process only selected documents; one extraction and one correction pass, then manual handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Product positioning and customer problems appear in varied prose that fixed field mapping cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Ask the customer about objectives, constraints, problems and business practices.
Consolidate verified research and discovery notes into a customer brief.
Resolve gaps and decide which customer needs should guide the sales approach.

tasks.design: Configure an account view in the {CRM} and run a bounded extraction loop over authorised material in the {DOCS}. The seller reviews the research and conducts discovery, capturing answers in structured fields; deterministic assembly produces a client brief for the seller's final judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer knowledge is split between records, documents and conversations. Reading prose and reconciling old briefs has resisted simple field mapping.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views handle structured history, while bounded extraction produces source-linked notes. AI-assisted coding makes the document and record connections cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may withhold constraints or describe symptoms rather than underlying needs. GDPR purpose limitation, data minimisation and access restrictions constrain reuse of customer information.
tasks.human_edge: Ask sensitive follow-up questions, recognise commercial subtext and distinguish a customer's stated request from their actual problem.

ambition.what: Provide a pre-campaign discovery brief covering objectives, constraints and unresolved measurement questions.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time reconstructing account history and more time testing assumptions with the customer. They gain a stronger basis for qualification decisions within their existing remit.

reach.task: Qualify whether a customer problem matches the service offered.
reach.learn: Discovery interviewing, qualification criteria and evidence-based disqualification.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales documents lead research and fit assessment; this supports research assistance, not reliable diagnosis of customer needs.
Source-linked extraction and deterministic brief assembly are plausible designs; no task-specific measured case is supplied.

assumptions: Customer-authorised documents and campaign history are available.
Discovery remains a substantial human conversation, consistent with the supplied priors.
The seller captures discovery answers in structured fields, allowing brief assembly without another model loop.
Build ranges exclude elapsed waits for data access or consultation.
unknowns: Where account history and customer materials are stored.
Whether document permissions and customer identity links are reliable.
Which data uses have a lawful basis and compatible purpose.
Whether national employee consultation rules apply to the proposed workflow.
research_questions: How often do past briefs contradict current customer statements?
Can extraction identify material gaps without adding irrelevant questions?
Which discovery fields are useful enough to justify structured capture?
new_work: Check extracted facts, source dates and contradictions.
Resolve ambiguous customer identities and document permissions.
Maintain the discovery fields and brief template.
Remove stale or unnecessary personal information.

tasks.short: Calculate advertising estimates and explain their price, assumptions and conditions to customers.

steps.what: Read the customer's advertising request and identify missing specifications.

loop.input: Customer email and attached advertising specifications.
loop.output: Structured requested formats, quantities, dates, budget and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types, units and catalogue identifiers; link extracted values to source text.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ambiguous specifications return to the seller without inferred values.
loop.why_not_simpler: Email requests use inconsistent language and attachments; fixed parsing cannot reliably map them to quote fields.

steps.what: Clarify formats, dates, quantities and budget with the customer.
Check the rate card for relevant formats, quantities and production charges.
Check placement availability and delivery constraints in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate the estimate, including discounts, production charges and applicable taxes.
Approve any discount or commercial term outside delegated limits.
Prepare the customer estimate with prices, validity dates, assumptions and exclusions.
Check and send the estimate with an explanation of its assumptions.

tasks.design: Configure a price catalogue and estimate templates in the {CRM}, with a deterministic calculator and a read-only availability connection to the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded loop extracts emailed requests; the seller confirms specifications, exceptions route through the {WORKFLOW}, and approved estimates are sent through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates, placement availability and discount decisions are disconnected. Variable customer requests create manual rekeying before otherwise routine arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Most of the solution uses established catalogue, calculation and approval patterns. AI-assisted coding lowers integration effort; a small extraction loop handles free-text requests.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke packages, negotiated rates and fast-changing inventory need careful versioning. Availability checks do not reserve inventory, and an estimate must make that distinction clear.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify what the customer actually needs, negotiate fair commercial terms and decide whether an unusual concession is worthwhile.

ambition.what: Provide a same-conversation comparison of three feasible advertising packages.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time calculating and assembling estimates and more time comparing options with the customer. Existing discount limits remain the basis for decision rights.

reach.task: Validate an accepted estimate before creating the advertising order.
reach.learn: Placement identifiers, production deadlines, order completeness and billing handoff requirements.

evidence.claim: Agentforce for Revenue is described as building a quote from a typed sentence.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks in its own sales team; the digest gives no baseline or period.
A rate-card calculator with discount limits can handle standard advertising estimates without model-based arithmetic.

assumptions: The baseline uses a spreadsheet rate card to connect sales and operations; system-native quoting is also common.
The approval step is an average across a mix of standard and exceptional estimates.
The {CRM} supports a configurable catalogue and document templates; otherwise a small deterministic records app is needed.
Prices, tax treatment, units and approval limits can be expressed as maintained rules.
Quoted build effort assumes one pricing scheme and one operations connection, without inventory reservation.
unknowns: Whether rates and discounts already exist in a configurable quoting module.
How much seller time is actually spent calculating versus discussing estimates.
Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} exposes reliable availability data.
Which packages require bespoke pricing or production review.
Who can approve discounts and how long estimates remain valid.
Which access approvals and national employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can historical estimates be reproduced exactly from versioned pricing rules?
Which missing specifications most often cause rework?
What availability freshness is sufficient for a non-binding estimate?
new_work: Maintain versioned prices, tax rules and discount limits.
Review extracted specifications and final customer estimates.
Handle bespoke packages and unavailable inventory.
Monitor failed connections and stale availability data.
Test pricing changes against representative historical estimates.

role.altitude: The advertising sales agent's week shifts from reconstructing account facts and assembling materials toward discovery, persuasive conversations and commercial judgement. Better preparation supports existing authority; broader pricing or account rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Sales manager: stakeholder planning and commercial exception assessment.
Sales engineer: advertising measurement and delivery feasibility.
Sales representative of services: structured discovery and qualification.
Order clerk: clean conversion from accepted estimate to executable order.
skills_to_grow: Interpret campaign evidence without promising unsupported outcomes.
Conduct discovery that exposes objectives, constraints and buying dynamics.
Compare advertising packages using versioned prices and realistic assumptions.
Review source-linked drafts and recognise missing or conflicting evidence.
Translate customer commitments into complete operational specifications.
role.ambitious_version: Offer smaller advertisers a joined discovery, package-comparison and campaign-review service using the same reusable account facts, evidence and pricing rules.
